items.title: Static spherical Einstein-fluid model with a supplied equation of state
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the countable-choice convention ZF+$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ used by the exact geometry supplier [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Use its product spacetime, areal radius $r$, time coordinate $x^0=ct$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and static metric
$$g=-e^{2\phi(r)}(dx^0)^2+b(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma,$$
where $\gamma$ is the unit round metric, $b(r)>0$, and the metric coefficients are independent of $x^0$. Here $x^0$ and $r$ are in metres, $\phi$ and $b$ are dimensionless, $G>0$ is in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and $c>0$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, as in [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. The static unit fluid velocity is $u=e^{-\phi}\partial_{x^0}$.

For an open pressure interval $I_P\subset(0,\infty)$, supply a $C^\infty$ constitutive function $\mathcal E:I_P\to(0,\infty)$, with pressure and energy-density values both in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. A pressure profile $P(r)$ has rest energy density $\varepsilon(r)=\mathcal E(P(r))$. Adopt the $\Lambda=0$ Einstein field equation
$$G^a{}_b=\frac{8\pi G}{c^4}T^a{}_b,\qquad T^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(-\varepsilon(r),P(r),P(r),P(r)),$$
with the signed curvature and Einstein-tensor conventions of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Thus “perfect fluid” here means exactly this static isotropic rest-frame stress tensor; the EOS is a supplied model input, not derived from gravity.

This is an adopted classical model and source of conditional predictions. The item asserts no observed star, measured EOS, global zero-pressure surface, causal finite-sound-speed law, or radial/dynamical stability. The cited treatments motivate the static-fluid and EOS conventions; the later local branch and constant-density results are established only by their displayed conditional arguments and mathematical suppliers.
items.physical_scope: Classical, static, isotropic, spherically symmetric Einstein gravity with Lambda=0, a supplied smooth positive energy-density-as-a-function-of-pressure relation, and positive radial metric coefficient b; no claim of a global surface, causal material dynamics, observed stellar matter, or stability.

items.title: Constructed regular-center local static TOV branch
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the adopted model [[post-tgr-static-spherical-fluid-preparation]] and its supplied $C^\infty$ positive EOS $\mathcal E:I_P\to(0,\infty)$ on an open pressure interval $I_P\subset(0,\infty)$. Let $P_c\subset I_P$ be a nonempty compact interval, let $\delta>0$ be such that its closed $\delta$-neighbourhood lies in $I_P$, and choose a central pressure $P_0\in P_c$ and a dimensionless central lapse $e^{\phi_c}>0$. Under the exact mathematical convention $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[thm-tgr-tov-regular-center-local-existence]], put $K=4\pi G/c^4$. There is a common $R_0>0$ and, for each $P_0\in P_c$, smooth even profiles $P,v$ on $[-R_0,R_0]$ satisfying
$$v(r)=K\int_0^1s^2\mathcal E(P(rs))\,ds,\qquad P(r)=P_0-\int_0^r t\frac{(\mathcal E(P(t))+P(t))(v(t)+KP(t))}{1-2t^2v(t)}\,dt,$$
with $P(0)=P_0$, $v(0)=K\mathcal E(P_0)/3$, $b(r):=1-2r^2v(r)\ge1/2$, and $P'(0)=v'(0)=0$. Defining
$$M(r)=\frac{c^2}{G}r^3v(r),\qquad \phi(r)=\phi_c+\int_0^r t\frac{v(t)+KP(t)}{1-2t^2v(t)}\,dt,$$
gives a positive-lapse $C^2$ metric center and a local solution of the adopted Einstein-fluid equations. On $r>0$ its equations are
$$M'=\frac{4\pi r^2\mathcal E(P)}{c^2},\qquad \phi'=\frac{GM/c^2+4\pi Gr^3P/c^4}{r^2b},\qquad P'=-\frac{G(\mathcal E(P)+P)(M+4\pi r^3P/c^2)}{c^2r^2b}.$$
No conclusion is made that the branch reaches a finite zero-pressure surface, remains horizon-free globally, or is dynamically stable.
items.physical_scope: Local branch around a regular center for a supplied smooth positive EOS and compact central-pressure range in the adopted classical static isotropic Lambda=0 model; no global surface, global horizon avoidance, realistic EOS, empirical claim, or dynamical stability.

items.title: Specified constant-density star and vacuum boundary model
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Within the adopted model [[post-tgr-static-spherical-fluid-preparation]], choose a constant rest mass density $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, so the constant rest energy density is $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Fix an areal boundary radius $R>0$ in metres, define $M_R=4\pi\rho_0R^3/3$ in kilograms and $u=2GM_R/(c^2R)$, and restrict the model parameters to $0<u<8/9$. Adopt the supplied equation of state $\mathcal E(P)=\varepsilon_0$, impose the boundary condition $P(R)=0$, and prescribe vacuum stress for $r\ge R$ with exterior mass $M_R$.

This is a constitutive and boundary preparation within the stated static Einstein-fluid model. The uniform-density relation is a model input; it is not a finite-sound-speed causal transport law. The range $0<u<8/9$ defines this selected branch and does not assert a general Buchdahl bound, a realistic stellar equation of state, an observed star, or stability.
items.physical_scope: Constant-energy-density specialization of the adopted static isotropic model, with prescribed areal radius, compactness 0<u<8/9, zero surface pressure, and a vacuum exterior; no finite-sound-speed constitutive dynamics, general compactness theorem, observed matter, or stability claim.

items.title: Supplied thermodynamic chart and gravitational entropy variation model
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ exactly as in [[def-tgr-spherical-entropy-constraint-functional]]. Adopt a separate static, spherically symmetric, isotropic $\Lambda=0$ Einstein-fluid preparation using the geometry and $(-,+,+,+)$, $x^0=ct$ conventions of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]], without a separate barotropic relation $\varepsilon=\mathcal E(P)$. The adopted field equation is $G^a{}_b=(8\pi G/c^4)T^a{}_b$ with $T^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(-\varepsilon(r),P(r),P(r),P(r))$ and the signed curvature convention in [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Fix a radius $R>0$, and supply a $C^2$ open state chart $\mathcal U\subset(0,\infty)^2$ with coordinates energy density $\varepsilon$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and fixed-composition marker number density $n$ in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. Supply $s\in C^2(\mathcal U,\mathbb R)$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ with $s_\varepsilon>0$, and define
$$\Theta:=1/s_\varepsilon,\qquad \mu:=-\Theta s_n,\qquad P:=\Theta s+\mu n-\varepsilon.$$
Assume this chart is compatible with the adopted material energy-per-marker function $e(v,\sigma_p)$ of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]: $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $\varepsilon=n e(1/n,s/n)$, and $\Theta=e_{\sigma_p}>0$ on the supplied chart. The symbols $\Theta,\mu,P$ respectively have units kelvins, joules, and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The local identities $d\varepsilon=\Theta\,ds+\mu\,dn$ and $dP=s\,d\Theta+n\,d\mu$ are those of the exact mathematical chart definition [[def-tgr-spherical-entropy-constraint-functional]].

For positive even $C^2$ profiles $(\varepsilon(r),n(r))$ with compact range in $\mathcal U$, define $M,b,S,N_b,E$ exactly by [[def-tgr-spherical-entropy-constraint-functional]] and require $b(r)\ge b_*>0$ on $[0,R]$. The adopted proper entropy and particle number are $S=4\pi\int_0^R s r^2b^{-1/2}dr$ and $N_b=4\pi\int_0^R n r^2b^{-1/2}dr$, while the constrained mass-energy is $E=c^2M(R)=4\pi\int_0^R\varepsilon r^2dr$. Restrict variations to the supplied positive-$b$ chart at fixed $R$ and fixed $E,N_b$, and choose the boundary time normalization $e^{\phi(R)}=\sqrt{b(R)}$.

This model supplies local material thermodynamics and a gravitational mass constraint as assumptions. Its variation problem is not an independent derivation of all Einstein equations. A stationary profile is only a first-variation critical point; no entropy maximum, existence of a maximizing profile, boundary vacuum matching, or physical observation is assumed.

items.title: Verified constant-density static star and vacuum exterior
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the constant-density preparation [[post-tgr-incompressible-star-preparation]] and the exact $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ mathematical convention used by [[thm-tgr-constant-density-star-verified]]. Put $a=\sqrt{1-u}$ and $B(r)=\sqrt{1-ur^2/R^2}$. For $0\le r\le R$, the adopted model has the explicit profiles
$$M(r)=M_R(r/R)^3,\quad b(r)=B(r)^2,\quad P(r)=\varepsilon_0\frac{B(r)-a}{3a-B(r)},\quad e^{\phi(r)}=\frac{3a-B(r)}2.$$
For $r\ge R$, set $M(r)=M_R$, $b(r)=1-2GM_R/(c^2r)$, $P(r)=0$, $\varepsilon(r)=0$, and $e^{\phi(r)}=\sqrt{b(r)}$. Then the interior is a regular static Einstein-fluid solution through the center, the exterior is vacuum, and the join at $r=R$ is $C^1$ and piecewise $C^2$ with no delta-supported surface stress. The central pressure is finite and equals $P(0)=\varepsilon_0(1-a)/(3a-1)$. This conclusion is specific to the constant-density branch $0<u<8/9$.
items.physical_scope: Exact constant-density family in the adopted static Lambda=0 model for 0<u<8/9, including regular center and explicit C1 piecewise-C2 vacuum matching; the bound is family-specific, with no realistic causal EOS, general Buchdahl conclusion, empirical claim, or stability result.

items.title: Constrained entropy criticality yields scoped TOV and Tolman–Klein relations
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the model preparation [[post-tgr-gravitating-entropy-variational-preparation]], including a positive even $C^2$ profile pair with compact state-chart range, fixed $R>0$, $b\ge b_*>0$, fixed constraints $E,N_b$, and boundary normalization $\phi(R)=\tfrac12\log b(R)$. Use the exact $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[thm-tgr-constrained-entropy-tov-criticality]]. An admissible profile curve is $C^1$ in the sup-norm space $C^0([0,R])^2$ on an open interval about zero, takes values in the even $C^2$ positive-b profile domain with range in a compact subset of the open state chart, and has a smooth derivative at zero compactly supported in $(0,R)$ and extended evenly at the center. Define constrained stationarity to mean that $S$ has zero derivative at the base profile along every such curve preserving both $E$ and $N_b$. Then constrained stationarity is equivalent to the existence of constants $\alpha,\Theta_K,\mu_K$ such that on $(0,R)$
$$\frac{\mu}{\Theta}=\alpha,\qquad \Theta e^\phi=\Theta_K,\qquad \mu e^\phi=\mu_K,$$
and the pressure obeys
$$P'=-(\varepsilon+P)\phi'=-\frac{G(\varepsilon+P)(M+4\pi r^3P/c^2)}{c^2r^2b}.$$
Here $\Theta_K=\Theta(R)\sqrt{b(R)}$ and $\mu_K=\mu(R)\sqrt{b(R)}$. This is a conditional first-variation result in the adopted model, not a claim that nature selects such a profile or that it is an entropy maximum.
items.physical_scope: First-variation equivalence on the supplied fixed-radius, positive-b, compatible C2 state chart with fixed mass-energy and particle number and the stated boundary clock; no entropy maximum, global equilibrium existence, vacuum matching, arbitrary EOS, empirical observation, or dynamical stability.

items.title: Selected finite bath and effective energy-exchange preparation
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use the finite relative Kepler subsystem and Gibbs-volume entropy convention of [[post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-preparation]], with $R>16r_0$. In that model, choose $E_G=-e_*$ with $A/R<e_*<A/(16r_0)$, strictly inside the energy branch, and restrict to an open interval $\mathcal I_G$ about $x_*=E_G$ whose energies stay in that interior. The supplied formula $\Omega(-e)=C e^{-3/2}J(er_0/A)$ has $J(\delta)=\int_\delta^1s^{1/2}(1-s)^{3/2}ds$ and $J'(\delta)=-\delta^{1/2}(1-\delta)^{3/2}$; because $\delta$ stays in $(0,1/16)$, this derivative is smooth there, so $J$, $\Omega$, and $S_G=k_B\log\Omega$ are $C^2$ on $\mathcal I_G$. The mathematical result [[thm-tgr-regulated-kepler-negative-capacity]] gives $T_G(x_*)=T_*>0$ and finite $C_G(x_*)<0$ on this branch; restrict $\mathcal I_G$ if necessary so these strict signs persist. For a physical Newtonian slow-motion interpretation, also retain the upstream condition $2A/(\mu r_0c^2)\le\delta_{\rm NR}\ll1$ for a stated tolerance $\delta_{\rm NR}$; the scalar exchange calculation itself uses only the explicitly adopted model.

As a separate finite bath, choose $C_b>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, reference energy $E_0$ in joules, reference temperature $T_{\rm ref}>0$ in kelvins, and entropy constant $S_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. For bath energy $E_b>E_0$, adopt
$$S_b(E_b)=C_b\log\!\left(\frac{E_b-E_0}{C_bT_{\rm ref}}\right)+S_0.$$
The logarithm argument is dimensionless, and this stipulated bath has $T_b=(dS_b/dE_b)^{-1}=(E_b-E_0)/C_b$ and constant heat capacity $C_b$. Fix total energy $E_{\rm tot}=x+E_b$, choose $E_b=E_0+C_bT_*$ to match the selected subsystem temperature, and restrict $0<C_b<|C_G(x_*)|$.

Finally adopt the effective scalar energy-exchange law
$$\dot x=L\,\frac{d}{dx}\bigl[S_G(x)+S_b(E_{\rm tot}-x)\bigr],\qquad L>0\ \mathrm{J\,K\,s^{-1}}.$$
The law is a selected one-dimensional model with time measured in seconds; it does not assert a relativistic transport equation or a mechanism for thermalization. The literature citations give gravitational-thermodynamic context only; the explicit bath and ODE are adopted here, and their mathematical consequences are proved conditionally by the linked local supplier.
items.physical_scope: A selected finite Gibbs-volume Kepler subsystem with negative capacity, a finite logarithmic-entropy bath with positive constant capacity, conserved total energy, a matched-temperature point, and the separately adopted scalar exchange ODE, with the upstream slow-motion bound retained for any Newtonian physical-applicability claim; not causal relativistic transport, generic stellar stability, empirical thermalization, or an observed reservoir.

items.title: Finite bath stabilizes the selected negative-capacity exchange model
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the finite-bath preparation [[post-tgr-finite-bath-exchange-preparation]], which supplies $C^2$ subsystem and bath entropies on open energy intervals, with subsystem temperature $T_*>0$, finite capacity $C_G<0$, bath capacity $C_b$ satisfying $0<C_b<|C_G|$, conserved total energy, and exchange law $\dot x=L S_{\rm tot}'(x)$ for $L>0$. At the matched-temperature point $x_*$,
$$S_{\rm tot}''(x_*)=-\frac1{T_*^2}\left(\frac1{C_G}+\frac1{C_b}\right)<0.$$
Consequently $x_*$ is a strict local entropy maximum in this energy-exchange direction, the adopted ODE has a forward-invariant local basin with exponential attraction to $x_*$, and along each solution $dS_{\rm tot}/dt=L(S_{\rm tot}')^2\ge0$. These are properties of the selected scalar exchange model only.
items.physical_scope: Local stability and exponential attraction only for the adopted scalar finite-bath exchange ODE at a matched-temperature point with C_G<0 and 0<C_b<|C_G|, retaining the upstream slow-motion condition for any Newtonian physical-applicability claim; no generic GR-fluid stability, causal transport law, empirical thermalization, or observation.

items.title: Half-compactness constant-density Einstein star
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Specialize the constant-density family of [[pthm-tgr-static-constant-density-star]] to $u=1/2$. Then
$$a=\frac1{\sqrt2},\qquad \frac{P(0)}{\varepsilon_0}=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{3-\sqrt2}\in(0,1),\qquad e^{\phi(0)}=\frac{3/\sqrt2-1}{2}>0.$$
At the surface, $b(R)=1/2$ and $e^{\phi(R)}=1/\sqrt2$. The prescribed vacuum exterior has $M=M_R$, $b(r)=1-R/(2r)$ and $e^{\phi(r)}=\sqrt{b(r)}$ for $r\ge R$.
items.physical_scope: The explicit constant-density family at u=1/2, with its adopted vacuum exterior; not an observed star, realistic EOS, or generic compactness result.

items.statement:

In the adopted scalar exchange model, the common-temperature state is a strict local entropy maximum and is locally exponentially attracting; its entropy curvature is
$$S_{\rm tot}''(x_*)=-\frac1{T_*^2|C_G|}<0.$$
